Q: Converting a data set into a data frame A:

There is

collapse::unlist2d(l=df$x)

e.g.

> collapse::unlist2d(l=df$x)  |>  
+   head()
  .id Consumption    Income
1   1   1.2956003 1.3494292
2   1   0.8485697 1.3218216
3   1   0.3185874 0.1642931
4   1   1.5231161 1.3339185
5   1   0.7618668 1.1741444
6   2   0.8480480 2.3678244

With idcols-argument you can specify the name. {collapse} is generally considered a rapidfly fast package, it also ships collapse::pivot-function for reshaping.

If the group column (.id) is not needed, simply

do.call(what='rbind', args=df$x) |> 
  as.data.frame()

Edit

If needed, I tend to use a Map + [<- construct like

lapply(df$x, data.frame) |> 
  ( \(.) Map(`[<-`, ., '.id', value=seq_along(df$x)) )() |> 
  do.call(what='rbind')

For wide format

lapply(df$x, data.frame) |> 
  do.call(what='cbind') |> 
  data.frame(check.names=TRUE)

might be enough.

Notes

  1. Please note that df <- <sth> masks stats::df- function which ships with R Core. Therefore, I recommend to assign to either metasyntactic variable names, e.g. foobar, foo, bar, baz, quux, xyzzy, ...,--personally I like .data, x, X which is rather R-specific--or something data-specific, e.g. cshd for cross-sectional household data.

  2. Where does the data come from. You might have an important issue and currently we are solving an XY-problem.

  3. Some tidy data references would encourage you to keep the data in long format.
